Bulira, Ocaima, Behuni (Beuni, Biuni), Ombecho, Anaitoma, Totumo, Natagaima, Pana (Pamao), Guarro, Hamay, Zeraco, Lucira,'' and ''Tonuro''. ==Classification== A small vocabulary list was collected in 1943; only 30 Pijao words and expressions are known.{{Cn|date=May 2025}} The few words which resemble [[Carib languages|Carib]] are thought to be loans; toponyms in Pijao country are also Carib. Durbin & Seijas (1973) did not detect significant connections between Pijao and other unclassified languages of the area: [[unclassified language of South America#Colima|Colima]], [[Muzo language|Muzo]], [[Pantagora language|Pantágora]], and [[Panche language|Panche]], but these are even more poorly attested than Pijao.{{Sfn|Durbin|Seijas|1973}} Jolkesky (2016) also notes that there are lexical similarities with the [[Witoto-Okaina languages]].{{cite thesis|last=Jolkesky |first=Marcelo Pinho de Valhery |date=2016
